claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
The splashdown marks the end of the crewed lunar flyby mission.
Live coverage is on NASA+ and major streaming platforms starting around 6:30 p.m. EDT.
The crew module separates from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT.
The capsule enters Earth's atmosphere at 7:53 p.m. EDT.
The capsule's atmospheric entry causes a brief communication blackout.
The mission marks the first crewed lunar mission in over 50 years.
The crew is testing systems for future lunar landings.
